title: Longitudinal KV-prefix cache drift & throughput benchmarking harness
creator: Asha Patel
description: Build a reproducible, longitudinal load-test harness focused on KV-prefix caching behavior under realistic prefix distributions. The harness will measure tokens/sec, p95 generation latency, memory utilization, and cache hit-rate over sustained runs to detect drift or regressions introduced by runtime changes (kernel swaps, batching adjustments, quantization profiles, eviction heuristics). The goal is to detect >10% p95 regressions or >7% drop in effective hit-rate within 24-hour rolling windows and to provide deterministic A/B comparisons between code branches and config variants.
acceptance_criteria: Reusable harness that can run in CI and on dedicated perf driver hosts
Collects and persists per-second metrics: tokens/sec, p95, p50, tail latencies (p95/p99), heap and GPU memory, KV cache hit/miss counts, and KV cache footprint
Automatic regression detection rules: flag if p95 increases by >=10% or effective hit-rate drops >=7% relative to baseline within 24h
Dashboards and nightly automation that runs baseline + candidate and posts diffs to PRs
Instrumentation added to runtime to export cache eviction counters and prefix distribution histograms
measurement_plan: Workload generation: mix of synthetic prefix-heavy traces (70% prefix repeats) and production-sampled traces (30%) from console-sampled prompts
Run durations: short smoke (30m), medium (4h), and long (24h) to capture steady-state behaviors

Metrics to record: tokens/sec, requests/sec, p95/p99 latency for generation endpoint, prefix-cache hit-rate, absolute cache entries, DRAM heap used, GPU memory used, CPU util per core, and tail latency percentiles
Environments: baseline branch (main), candidate branch, quantized model variant, and cached-disabled control
A/B approach: parallel runs on identical host types, seeded RNGs for deterministic generation, and synchronized start times for fair comparison
tasks: Design harness API and CLI for workload parameters (--prefix-dist, --concurrency, --seq-len, --duration)
Implement synthetic workload generator and connector to Redwood request router for direct runtime calls
Add telemetry hooks: KV cache evictions, prefix histogram snapshots, and per-request cache-hit tags
Integrate with observability stack (Prometheus metrics + Grafana dashboard + cloud storage for long-term traces)
Create regression detection lambda that compares candidate vs baseline and posts PR comments
Run baseline suite on dedicated perf pool and record canonical baselines for two host classes (g5.2xlarge and a100-40gb equivalent)
Document runbook and add CI job that triggers medium run on release branches
run_results: 2025-02-15 4h run (baseline on g5): tokens/sec=14200, p50=18ms, p95=96ms, p99=210ms, kv-hit=82.3%, mem_rss=9.8GB, gpu_mem=22.3GB
2025-02-16 4h run (candidate: kernel-sched-change): tokens/sec=13900, p50=19ms, p95=109ms (+13.5%), p99=225ms, kv-hit=80.9% (-1.7pp), mem_rss=10.1GB
2025-02-18 24h run (long-run quantized variant): tokens/sec=15050, p50=22ms, p95=118ms (+22.9% vs baseline), kv-hit=75.6% (-6.7pp), mem_rss=6.2GB, gpu_mem=19.8GB

Interpretation: the kernel-schedule change caused >10% p95 regression on medium run triggering automated alert. Quantized variant reduced memory but exhibited both increased p95 and lower hit-rate, likely due to increased cache miss amplification and different micro-kernel path latencies. Follow-up profiling required to correlate eviction patterns with tail latency spikes.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Synthetic workload may not reflect production prefix correlations — Mitigation: blend with sampled production traces and validate histograms
Risk: Long-run tests consume perf pool capacity — Mitigation: schedule nightly on isolated perf hosts and limit concurrency during business hours
Risk: False positives from transient infra noise — Mitigation: require sustained deviation over rolling 1h and 24h windows before alerting
